description: Zaanhof (BAG 1919, H.J.M. Walenkamp), the courtyard's 6 m two-dwelling fronts: two brick storeys, a wide window axis and a narrow one over a round-arched door at the party wall; over the wide axis a tall pointed gable rendered white from the first-floor head up, its yellow bargeboards on a red-tile roof, an attic light in it; beside it a small flat-roofed dormer over the door axis; yellow window frames, small-paned top lights; mirrored in pairs so the arched doors meet at every second party wall

white-gable.note: a pointed gable over the wide axis, apex 11.5 m from the 7.5 m eaves, an attic light at 7.7-9.0 m. The small flat-roofed dormer over the door axis (zaanhof-125-134 strip, Zaanhof 131: 1.45 m wide from 4.4 m to the party wall, gutter 7.3 m to top 8.75 m; 3DBAG flat tops 9.2-9.4 m, paired with the neighbour's across the party wall) is still left out: tried on the recipe roof 2026-10-24, a kit dormer standing at the gutter fails the GLB audit (flat style: its trim cheeks cross the 56-degree roof plane; box style: its open front is judged against the facade wall 0.35 m in front, whose silhouette ends at the eaves). Rise 0.9 storey (2026-10-24): bargeboard top 3.75-3.8 m over the gable foot on both strips (zaanhof-1-20 Zaanhof 19: foot 7.65, apex 11.4 m; zaanhof-125-134 Zaanhof 133: 7.2, 11.0 m), under the 3DBAG main ridge.

door-left.note: the round-arched door at the party wall (rectified 1.5 m wide, apex 2.85 m); the neighbour's arched door beside it

roof.evidence: 3DBAG LoD2.2 over all 30 Zaanhof pands (scripts/block-face/faces/zaanhof-*/pands/*/facts.json, 2026-10-24): a long saddle along the street, front slope 55-57 deg from 7.2-7.6 m to a ridge at 11.6-11.8 m, back slope 37-38 deg down to 6.4-6.8 m; behind every white gable two cross-roof planes at 53-58 deg up to 10.4-10.9 m (the gable is the end of a cross roof, its apex under the main ridge); flat dormer tops at 9.2-9.4 m. The strips agree: tiles rise behind the dormers to above the gable apex (zaanhof-125-134 strip, Zaanhof 133). rearPitchDeg 34 rather than 3DBAG's 38: the kit's rear face ends at the front eaves height (7.6 m; 3DBAG 6.4-6.8 m), and at 34 deg the faces of the shallowest pand (8.9 m deep) still reach the 11.6 m ridge over a flat strip of at most 0.7 m on the deepest.

match.note: the Zaanhof courtyard (1919); the 1934 infill at Zaanhof 85-89 is another design

rhythm.bays: a narrow door axis and a wide window axis
rhythm.windowsPerStorey: ground: arched door + 1 wide | 1: 1 narrow + 1 wide | attic: 1 gable light + 1 flat dormer over the door axis (the dormer not drawn, see crowns.white-gable.note)
rhythm.symmetry: mirrored in pairs: the arched doors meet on every second party wall, the gables on the others
rhythm.groundFloor: round-arched door at the party wall, one wide window
rhythm.roofline: pointed white gable over the wide axis (the end of a cross roof), a flat dormer over the door axis (not drawn), long red-tile saddle along the street

evidence.citation: strip.jpg 2021-03-19 (40 px/m, camera 2.1 m), ruler crop 7-22 m: brick to 6.6 m, white render to the 7.5 m eaves and up the gable to 11.5 m; wide windows 8.55-11.3 m at 0.65-2.85 and 4.1-6.05 m; narrow first-floor window 1.0 m; arched doors 1.5 m wide, apex 2.85 m, paired at the party wall; attic light 9.3-10.7 m at 7.7-9.0 m

notes: Palette: the type palette (match.measuredWall false): half of each front is white render and the 2021 strips are sunlit past the trim white point (render #f5f5ed-#fefefe, clipped), so the strip wall reads #cfaa82-#dbb185 brick-and-mortar for a red-brown brick. 2026-10-24: brick #a57a5c (was #9c6a52, 15 deg too red against both photos): the overcast 2017-04-24 crop of Zaanhof 19 (pand-reference all-walls, 0363100012107452 w01-249) reads brick #554438 under render #9c9b92, white-balanced to the render's #f2efe6 that is #846a57 (hue 23 deg); the sunlit 2021 strip's hue is 32 deg. Hue taken between them, lightness kept a step above the old palette (the city reads too dark).
